sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — of Uragasaurus consists of a single anterior dorsal vertebra that was flattened from front to back due to taphonomic compression.
This bone is distinguished from other mamenchisaurids by a teardrop-shaped pneumatic fossa at the tip of the transverse processes.
Fossils were found in the lower Phu Kradung Formation in Kalasin Province, northeastern Thailand, and the species was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Apirut Nilpanapan and colleagues.
The holotype is currently housed at Mahasarakham University under the accession number PRC 460.
This discovery marks the first named member of the family Mamenchisauridae from Thailand.
While Uragasaurus itself is known only from a vertebra, its relatives are characterized by greatly elongated necks.
Uragasaurus belongs to the class Saurischia and is classified as a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur, with the parent group being the family Mamenchisauridae.
Phylogenetic analysis places Uragasaurus as an early-diverging member of Mamenchisauridae, after Tienshanosaurus and before Qijianglong.
The animal lived between 149.2 and 137.05 million years ago during the Tithonian to Berriasian stages.

It is debated whether other fossil fragments found near the holotype belong to Uragasaurus because they lack diagnostic features, and the phylogenetic relationships of Uragasaurus are weakly supported due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil material.
